reasoning.text: The render passes both acceptance tests: the ISO reads instantly as an open-frame FPGA NTT card — eight blue interleaved BRAM banks on the -Z edge, the copper DSP-multiplier column and the symmetric dark/brushed add-sub pairs in an open rail-and-floor frame, the brass twiddle broadcast rail on top, the two-member Barrett reduction spine on +X, and the exploded radix-4 BU plus ten-fin heatsink lifted clear; FRONT and SIDE confirm every part sits on the ground line with no floaters and no opaque block swallowing a subsystem. The only visible defect is in TOP/plan: the exploded heatsink baseplate (x=4.6, z=0, depth 4.0) overlays the inner halves of the twiddle ROM and address-generation unit at z=+/-2.5, slightly costing plan-view legibility, and the heatsink sits offset to +X rather than over the die center it claims to cover. Critically, the remaining deficit is not visual at all — it is source fidelity: the bank-index b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8, the crossbar per-stage permutation sigma_s, the twiddle-ROM address function, DIT/DIF direction, the radix-4 fused schedule and the per-stage cycle counts are all reproduction-pinned values, not transcriptions of CFNTT Sec. III, and the prompt forbids inventing replacements for them here. The score has plateaued; buildability is capped at 16 by those un-transcribed source facts, which require the paper PDF.
gaps: Source fidelity (needs the paper PDF): transcribe CFNTT's actual conflict-free bank-index b(i) and offset o(i) from Sec. III; the current (i+(i>>3)) mod 8 map is injective but collides for radix-2 strides 2^6..2^9, so crossbar_network/bram/addr_gen_unit 'no-conflict' claims are an approximation. Do NOT invent a replacement — pin from source.

Source fidelity: the crossbar per-stage permutation sigma_s (logical operand index -> physical bank/lane port) is a reproduction rotation map in crossbar_network.spec; transcribe the paper's actual routing.
Source fidelity: confirm the twiddle-ROM address function f(stage s, block index) and the negacyclic low/high-half storage layout in twiddle_rom against the source.
Source fidelity: confirm DIT vs DIF and the global butterfly/stage ordering in schedule_controller (currently a reproduction choice).

Source fidelity: confirm the radix-4 fusion mapping (which two radix-2 stages fuse per BU, j-rotator sign convention) and the schedule that yields the quoted 33%/20% op savings in config_radix_selector/r4_fuse_* — still improvised.
Source fidelity: the FSM per-stage cycle counts and the 9-cycle/lane pipeline latency in schedule_controller/spec are reconstructed defaults, not transcribed; reconcile against the paper.
Source fidelity: primitive-root generator g=11, psi=1945, omega=10302, N^-1=12277 and the full twiddle table are reproduction-pinned to q=12289; confirm the modulus and root against the source.
Source fidelity: the modular adder/subtractor reduction policy (conditional +/-q correction count) in mod_red_subshift needs source confirmation.

Visualization (closeable next pass, low risk): in TOP/plan the exploded heatsink baseplate (z depth 4.0) overlays the inner halves of twiddle_rom and addr_gen_unit at z=+/-2.5; consider narrowing the heatsink depth or nudging it so both control blocks stay fully visible from above, and reconcile its +X offset with its 'covers the whole die' role.

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); the crossbar applies read permutation sigma_s where operand-a of lane L is fetched from bank (L - s) mod 8 and operand-b from bank (L - s + R_s) mod 8 with R_s = ((2^s)>>3)+1; the write-back applies the inverse sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which b(i) is intended to spread over 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle

before.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. KNOWN REPRODUCTION GAP: the candidate map b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 is conflict-free for radix-2 stages s=0..5 (operand distance 2^s gives b(i+2^s)=b(i)+(2^(s-3) mod 8), which is nonzero for s<6), but it COLLIDES for strides 2^6/2^7/2^8/2^9 (s=6..9), where 2^(s-3)≡0 mod 8 forces b(i+2^s)=b(i) so the two operands of one butterfly land in the same bank. This map therefore does NOT yet reproduce the paper's headline conflict-free bank/offset functions (CFNTT Sec. III), which must be transcribed from the source; the permutation sigma_s recorded here is the matching reproduction candidate, not the verified paper map.

after.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.

Floor depth 8.8 m fully contains the outermost add/sub operators (z=±4.30) within its ±4.4 edge.

fields.before: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels, and spans east to x=3.3 to meet the relocated reduction member.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

before.notes: Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1. KNOWN REPRODUCTION GAP: the source's actual twiddle-ROM address function f(stage s, block) and its low/high-half negacyclic storage layout are not transcribed and remain to be taken from CFNTT.

params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle
params.radix2_butterfly: Cooley-Tukey: with w=omega^k, u=x0, v=w*x1 -> y0=(u+v) mod q, y1=(u-v) mod q
params.twiddles_per_radix4_BU: 3 nontrivial twiddles W1=w, W2=w^2, W3=w^3 (so 3 modular mults); j=psi^512 is a stored constant rotator, not a fetched twiddle
params.op_counts: radix-4 BU = 3 modular mults + 8 modular add/sub, vs two radix-2 stages = 4 mults + 8 add/sub on the same 4 points; the paper's rearranged schedule realizes 33% fewer modular multiplications and 20% fewer modular add/sub overall

before.notes: Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs radix-2; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing. The radix-4 equations and 3-twiddle assignment recorded here are the basis of the quantified op savings; the precise mapping of which two radix-2 stages fuse per BU and the j-rotator sign convention are reproduction-chosen and pending source confirmation.

transitions: IDLE -> LOAD  [host start pulse]
LOAD -> STAGE_LOOP  [coefficient vector resident in banks]
STAGE_LOOP -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [enter next twiddle-sharing block]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
BUTTERFLY -> REDUCE  [lane products valid]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
STAGE_LOOP -> DRAIN  [forward-only transform done]
INTT_STAGE_LOOP -> SCALE_N_INV  [inverse stages done]
SCALE_N_INV -> DRAIN  [coefficients scaled by N^-1]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

loop_bounds.stages_radix4: S4 = log4(N) = 5 passes, each fusing two radix-2 stages
loop_bounds.blocks_per_stage: N / 2^(s+1) groups at stage s, each sharing one twiddle factor

ops: for s in stages: for block in groups_sharing_one_twiddle: { fetch w once; parallel for bu in 0..7: butterfly(bu) }
before.notes: The factor-constant inner block is what lets one twiddle fetch be reused across all 8 lanes. The transition table and loop bounds here are reconstructed; the source asserts the 33%/20% savings only as a property and does not publish its state machine. DECIMATION CONVENTION IS A REPRODUCTION CHOICE: this schedule assumes decimation-in-time (DIT), with natural-order input placed by the conflict-free map and natural-order output (no bit-reversal stage). The source does not state DIT vs DIF, the global butterfly/stage ordering, or its per-stage cycle counts; those remain to be transcribed from CFNTT before the timing is faithful.
